title: How an array measures DNA

blocks.what_we_do: Separate a fluorescence measurement from a genotype call.
blocks.why: An array measures fluorescent signals from DNA hybridising to probes. Probes are short DNA sequences designed to recognise selected sites. Intensities from two channels tend to form clusters representing the two homozygotes and the heterozygote. A calling algorithm assigns a genotype or leaves the call missing. Signal strength is a measurement, not an allele count. Poor separation, background signal and unusual DNA mixtures can produce uncertain calls.
blocks.you_need: The array annotation from 1.1; the final report examples supplied at 0.5.

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
A simulated Final Report header and the start of its data section. The supplied reports have genotype calls and GC scores; they do not contain raw intensity data, so this exercise cannot redraw cluster plots.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows with the supplied simulated dataset.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Can a low-quality fluorescence measurement be treated as a confidently observed missing allele?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Missing means no accepted genotype call; it is not a biological allele.

</details>
